role: Build record of the runner bwx12: compiler, flags, self-test result, sha256 digests.
purpose: build12.sh wrote this file on CRB on 2026-11-15, when it built the runner bwx12. The file records the machine load, the compiler and its flags, the result of the self-test, the calls inside the timed functions of the trial mode, the placement of five functions, and the sha256 digest of the bwx12 binary that the whole-chip test ran.

main_flow.step: A line that starts with `##` is written by build12.sh. Lines 17 to 23 are the direct output of `sha256sum`.
Read where and when the build ran, and with which compiler and flags.
Read the compiler messages between the two marker lines. Here there is none.
Read the result of the self-test of the new binary.
Read which functions the two timed functions of the trial mode call.
Read where five functions start, modulo 64, in bwx12 and in three earlier binaries (bwx8 has four of the five).
Read the sha256 digests of the inputs, of the binary (line 20) and of three output files.
Read the load and the time at the end of the build.

behavior_notes: The scripts of the whole-chip test do not build bwx12. They run a binary with the digest of this build: go.sh and go2.sh stop unless the sha256 digest of the binary equals the value of line 20 [Ref3]. The env.txt files of the nine bwx12 result folders of the whole-chip test hold the same digest [Ref8].

This file records the build of bwx12 only. Part A of the whole-chip test runs the binaries bw_old and bw_new, not bwx12. The script run_kernels.sh built them on 2026-11-13 with the first seven flags of line 3 [Ref2]. Its three records of that day hold the same two sha256 digests for them [Ref2]. ra.sh, the script of part A, holds the same two digests. It stops if a binary has another digest [Ref9].

build12.sh stops with a non-zero exit status before it writes line 16 when the compile fails (status 5), when the self-test fails (status 4), or when the branch targets of a timed function of the trial mode fail the check behind lines 7 and 8 (status 6). So a file that has lines 16 to 24 passed these three checks [Ref1].
The comparisons of lines 11, 13 and 15 are a record only. `DIFFERS` would not stop the build [Ref1].

Lines 7 to 15 concern mostly the trial mode of bwx12. The bwx12 processes of the whole-chip test use the interval mode, in which the function `worker` times the kernels [Ref4]. No line of this file describes `worker`.

Insufficient data: whether `worker` reaches the kernels through the copy of `call` whose start address modulo 64 line 9 gives, or through a copy that gcc put inside `worker`. The machine code of `worker` in the binary would resolve it. No saved listing holds it.

Check made for this page on 2026-11-21 with `sha256sum`: the local copies of bwx12.c, bwx12_selftest.c, build12.sh, listing.txt, offsets.tsv and seq-listing.txt have the digests of lines 17 to 19 and 21 to 23. The binary is not in the folder of bwx12.c or in this folder, so line 20 was not computed again.

words.def: the Arm reference server under test. It has 128 CPUs.
the inner loop of the benchmark that reads memory. On this page "kernel" means this loop. The operating system kernel is always written "Linux kernel".
later runner programs for the same loops. They print one row per thread. bwx12 is the runner of the 2026-11-15 investigation. bwx11 and bwx are older versions.
two more earlier versions of the runner program. build12.sh reads the symbol table of their accepted binaries.
the word of build12.sh for the binary of an earlier version (bwx8, bwx10, bwx11) that serves as the reference for a new build.
the benchmark and its two binaries of 2026-11-13. bw_old was built from the old source, bw_new from the new source.
the script that builds bwx12 on CRB and writes this file. It stands in the folder above this one.
the GNU C compiler.
the run `bwx12 --selftest`. It runs every kernel on test buffers and checks the trial mode. It prints one row with `pass` or `FAIL` per check.

the two modes of bwx12. Interval mode (option `--seq`): every thread runs a sequence of kernels, and each timed interval holds the calls of one kernel. The bwx12 processes of the whole-chip test use it. Trial mode (option `--trial`): one thread runs the trials of a plan file. The whole-chip test does not use it.
the two functions of the trial mode that run and time the kernels.
a function of the trial mode. It reads the hardware counters and the CPU time of the thread.
the function of bwx12.c that runs one kernel on a range of the buffer of a thread.
the function of bwx12.c that reads from /proc/self/smaps the size of each buffer and the part of it that uses huge pages (pages of 2 MiB).
the thread function of the interval mode. It reads the clock before and after the kernel calls of an interval.
the address or the function that a branch or call instruction goes to.
Arm branch instructions. `bl` calls a function at a fixed address. `blr` calls the function whose address a register holds. `b` jumps to a fixed address and keeps no return address.
a value that the compiled code stores on the stack at the start of a function and compares before the return. If the value changed, the code calls `__stack_chk_fail`.
the remainder after a division by 64. For an address it is the position inside a 64-byte block, from 0 to 63. bwx12.c counts one cache line as 64 bytes.
the start address of a function or a loop, modulo 64.
a command that lists the symbols of a binary: each function name with its address.
a command that prints the machine code of a binary as assembler text, one instruction per line with its address.
a checksum of 256 bits that the command `sha256sum` computes from the content of a file. It is printed as 64 hexadecimal digits. The scripts use it to check that a file is the expected one.
the number of tasks that are runnable or wait for disk input and output, averaged by Linux over the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes (file /proc/loadavg).
Coordinated Universal Time, the time scale without a local time zone.

scripts of the whole-chip test. go.sh is the driver of the run. go2.sh is a second driver that was added later for two more bwx12 processes. rx.sh starts one bwx12 process per line of a spec file (a file that holds, per process, a tag and the arguments of bwx12).

the file that rx.sh writes first into each result folder. It holds the time, the Linux kernel version, the load, the logins, the busiest processes, and a line `binary` with the path and the sha256 digest of the binary.

a process is one start of a benchmark binary. An interval is one timed measurement inside a process. bwx12 times a sequence of kernels and repeats the sequence: each repeat is a round (counted from 0), and the position is the place of a kernel in the sequence (counted from 0). In part A the round (1 or 2) is the round of the script: round 2 runs the processes in the reverse order.
the 120-thread part of the test of 2026-11-13, repeated with the same two binaries.
the run under review: the read test with 120 threads on CRB, run on 2026-11-17.
our runs use CPUs 0-119 only: 64 threads on mesh 0 plus 56 threads on mesh 1. Each thread reads its own buffer of 256 MiB from memory.
the two halves of the chip. CPUs 0-63 sit on mesh 0. CPUs 64-127 sit on mesh 1.

refs.what: the script that wrote this file. Line 37 sets the flags. The build scripts of bwx, bwx8, bwx10 and bwx11 (build.sh, build8.sh, build10.sh and build11.sh in the folders bwx-2026-11-13, bwx8-2026-11-14, bwx10-2026-11-15 and bwx11-2026-11-15) hold the same flags line. Lines 39-48 write lines 1 to 5, lines 50-55 write line 6, lines 83-99 write lines 7 and 8 and hold the exit with status 6, lines 107-151 write lines 9 to 15 (the comment on lines 101-106 says that a difference does not stop the build), lines 153-157 write lines 16 to 24.

lines 2 and 3 hold the compiler version and the flags of the bw_old and bw_new build. Lines 19 and 20 hold the sha256 digests of bw_old and bw_new. Line 19 of run_kernels.sh (folder kernels-2026-11-13) sets these flags, and lines 31-32 of that script build the two binaries. The script wrote two more records on that day: the probe.txt files of the folders kernels-20261113T181210Z and kernels-20261113T183218Z. Their lines 3, 19 and 20 hold the same flags and the same two digests.

line 13 holds the digest and line 23 checks the binary. go2.sh in the same folder does the same on its lines 10 and 19. rx.sh (folder w120-2026-11-15) checks the digest on line 8 and writes it to env.txt on line 10.

lines 143-147: the placement of a kernel needs the two flags. Line 253: the four kernel types. Line 459: the flag -fno-ipa-icf keeps both copies of a kernel. Lines 1440-1449: the unused bytes after the kernels, which keep the start of `call` and of the code after it at the same address modulo 64 as in bwx11, bwx10 and bwx8. Lines 1491-1509: `call` holds one kernel call per kernel type. Lines 1632-1735: `worker` calls `call` between the clock read that starts an interval (line 1688) and the clock read that ends it (line 1700 or line 1714). Lines 1967-2093: `tcount`, `timed_sequence`, `timed_sequence_hot`. Lines 2912-2914: only the option --trial starts the trial mode. Line 3111: `main` calls `read_smaps` between two intervals.

the machine code that build12.sh counted for lines 7 and 8. Each of the two functions holds 4 `blr` instructions, 2 `bl` to clock_gettime, one `bl` and one `b` to tcount, and one `bl` to __stack_chk_fail.

the saved output of the self-test: 852 lines, of which 457 are check rows that end with `pass`: 422 rows that start with a kernel name and 35 rows that start with `trial`. The last line is `# failures=0`.
lines 709-710 print the failure count and return 1 if it is above 0, else 0.
the files env.txt of the nine folders w120-T72L1 to L3, w120-T72C1 to C4, w120-T72I1 and I2: the line `binary` holds the digest of line 20.
the script of part A. Lines 16-20 check the sha256 digests of bw_old and bw_new and end the script with exit status 2 if one differs. Lines 17 and 18 hold the two values. Line 42 runs a binary.
